seoTitle: API Integration — Meaning and Example for Businesses
metaDescription: Two systems exchanging data automatically. Manual re-entry between systems is slow and produces mismatches nobody notices until reconciliation.
definition: An API integration lets two systems exchange data automatically — a POS sending sales to accounting software, or an aggregator pushing orders into a kitchen display — without anyone retyping anything.
bodyHtml:
Why API Integration matters

Manual re-entry between systems is slow and produces mismatches nobody notices until reconciliation. Integrations remove both, though they add a dependency to maintain.

How API Integration works in practice

Integrate the flows with real daily volume — orders in, sales out — and leave low-volume tasks manual. Every integration needs a plan for what happens when it silently stops working.

faq.question: Do I need an API for a small business?
faq.answer: Only where re-entry volume justifies it. Below that, a CSV export is usually enough.

faq.question: What breaks integrations most often?
faq.answer: Changed credentials and changed data formats on either side, which is why silent failures need monitoring.
